title: Z80 SCC channel registers
covers: the control registers of each channel of the Zilog SCC family: write registers WR0 to WR10 and their bits

rows.text: WR0 is the command register and the CRC reset code register.
WR0 takes slightly different forms depending on whether the SCC is a Z85X30 or a Z80X30.
Figure 5-1 shows the Z85X30 form of WR0, with register select bits in addition to the command and reset codes.
Figure 5-2 shows the Z80X30 form of WR0, which includes in Channel B only the address decoding select.
The bit description of WR0 is identical for both versions except where specified.
WR0 bits D7 and D6 are CRC Reset Codes 1 and 0; the capture prints the 0 as the letter O.
WR0 bits D5 to D3 are the Command Codes for the SCC.
On the Z85X30 WR0 stores D2-D0, the register pointer bits, which select registers 0 through 7; with the Point High command, registers 8 through 15 are selected.
In the multiplexed bus mode of the Z80X30, bit D2 must be programmed as 0.
In the multiplexed bus mode WR0 stores D1-D0, which select Shift Left (WR0 D1-D0 = 10) or Shift Right (11); the capture prints the 0 as the letter O.
WR1 is the control register for the various SCC interrupt and Wait/Request modes.
WR1 stores D7, WAIT/DMA Request Enable, and D6, WAIT/DMA Request Function; 0 selects the Wait function and 1 the Request function.
When D7 is 0 the selected function forces the /W//REQ pin into its inactive state, High for Request and floating for Wait; when 1, D6 sets the pin's activity.
In the Wait function, D6 = 0, the /W//REQ pin switches from floating to Low when the CPU attempts to transfer data before the SCC is ready.
In Request mode, D6 = 1, /W//REQ goes Low when the SCC is ready: for the transmit buffer if D5 is 0, for the receive buffer if D5 is 1.
A transmit request function is available on the /DTR//REQ pin, which allows full-duplex operation under DMA control for both channels.
The request function occurs only when the SCC is not selected; in synchronous or SDLC transmit mode the request pulses Low one PCLK cycle at the end of CRC transmission.
In Wait On Receive mode the wait pin is active if the CPU reads data not yet received; in Wait On Transmit mode if it writes to a full buffer.
WR1 stores D4-D3, the Receive Interrupt Mode: 00 disabled, 01 first character or special condition, 10 all characters or special condition, 11 special condition only.
With receive interrupts disabled the receiver cannot request an interrupt, though a special condition can still provide a unique vector status in RR2.
On first character or special condition, the receiver requests an interrupt for the first available or stored FIFO character or for a special condition; stripped sync characters cause none.
Special receive conditions are receiver overrun, framing error, end of frame, or parity error if selected; the data with the error stays in the Receive FIFO until an Error Reset.
A pending special receive condition remains set until an Error Reset command, a channel or hardware reset, or until receive interrupts are disabled.
The Receive Interrupt on First Character or Special Condition mode can be re-enabled by the Enable Rx Interrupt on Next Character command in WR0.
For the ESCC, the description of WR7' says how this function can be changed.
On all characters or special condition, every received character interrupts and a unique vector marks a special condition; overrun is always special, parity can be programmed as special.
In the all-characters mode, data characters with special receive conditions are not held in the Receive FIFO as they are in the other receive interrupt modes.
On special condition only, the receiver interrupts only on characters with a special condition, the error data staying in the Receive FIFO until an Error Reset command.
With a DMA, the special-condition mode lets the DMA be enabled before any character arrives, so the CPU need not treat the first character specially.
In SDLC mode with the SDLC Frame Status FIFO enabled, an EOF interrupts with the receive-data-available vector and the Receive FIFO is not locked.
WR1 stores D2, Parity Is Special Condition; when 1, a received character whose parity differs from the WR4 sense gives a Special Receive Condition; ignored if parity is disabled.
A special condition modifies the status of the interrupt vector stored in WR2, which can be placed on the data bus during an interrupt acknowledge cycle.
WR1 stores D1, Transmitter Interrupt Enable; when 1, the transmitter requests an interrupt whenever the transmit buffer becomes empty.
WR1 stores D0, the External/Status Master Interrupt Enable, which enables External/Status interrupts; WR15 holds the individual enables of their sources.
WR1 D0 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
MAME drives /W//REQ Low for a received character if D5 is 1, and for an empty transmit buffer if D5 is 0 and register 0x05 D3 enables the transmitter.
MAME's channel reset, z80scc_channel::device_reset, keeps WR1 D5 and D2 and clears every other bit, including D7-D6, D4-D3 and D1, with m_wr1 &= 0x24.
WR2 is the interrupt vector register.
Only one vector register exists in the SCC, and WR2 can be written through either channel.
The interrupt vector can be modified by status information, controlled by the Vector Includes Status and Status High/Status Low bits in WR9.
The bit positions of WR2 are shown in Figure 5-4.
MAME also copies the vector written to WR2 into read register 0x02 of both channels.
WR3 contains the control bits and parameters for the receiver logic, illustrated in Figure 5-5.
On the ESCC, with the Extended Read option enabled, WR3 may be read as RR9.
WR3 D7-D6 select the number of bits assembled as a received character: 00 five, 01 seven, 10 six, 11 eight.
The number of bits per character can be changed while a character is being assembled, but only before the programmed number of bits is reached.
Unused bits in the Received Data Register (RR8) are set to 1 in asynchronous modes.
In Synchronous and SDLC modes the SCC merely transfers an 8-bit section of the serial data stream to the Receive FIFO at the appropriate time.
WR3 stores D5, Auto Enables; when 1, /CTS becomes the transmitter enable and /DCD the receiver enable, after the Receiver Enable and Transmit Enable bits are set.
When Auto Enables is 0, the /DCD and /CTS pins are inputs to the corresponding status bits in Read Register 0.
The state of /DCD is ignored in Local Loopback mode, and the state of /CTS in both Auto Echo and Local Loopback modes.
WR3 stores D4, Enter Hunt Mode, which forces the comparison of sync characters or flags to assembled receive characters for the purpose of synchronization.
After reset the SCC automatically enters Hunt mode except in asynchronous mode, and again when an abort condition is received or the receiver is enabled.
On a flag or sync character match the Sync/Hunt bit in RR0 is reset and, if External/Status Interrupt Enable is set, an interrupt sequence starts.
WR3 stores D3, Receiver CRC Enable, which starts CRC calculation at the beginning of the last byte moved from the Receiver Shift register to the Receive FIFO.
To exclude a byte from the CRC calculation, reset this bit before the next byte is transferred; eight bits per character must then be selected.
This bit is internally set to 1 in SDLC mode, where the CRC covers all bits except inserted zeros, and it is ignored in asynchronous modes.
WR3 stores D2, Address Search Mode (SDLC); set in SDLC mode, it rejects messages whose address does not match WR6, and no receiver interrupts occur without a match.
The address matched is unique (1 in 256) or multiple (16 in 256), by the Sync Character Load Inhibit bit; FFH is always global; the bit is ignored outside SDLC.
WR3 stores D1, SYNC Character Load Inhibit; set outside SDLC mode, the SCC compares WR6 with the byte about to enter the FIFO and skips the load if equal.
That compare also occurs in asynchronous mode, and the SCC does not calculate CRC on bytes stripped this way.
With the 6-bit sync option in Monosync mode the compare still spans eight bits, so WR6 is programmed for proper operation.
In SDLC mode with this bit set, only the four high bits of WR6 must match the address, so the SCC can receive from up to 16 sources.
With the 6-bit sync option and this bit set, all sync characters except the one before the data are stripped; in Bisync mode the bit is ignored.
The address field in the frame is still eight bits long, and address FFH is always recognized as a global address.
The bit is ignored in SDLC mode if Address Search mode has not been selected.
WR3 stores D0, Receiver Enable; when set to 1, receiver operation begins.
The Receiver Enable bit should be set only after all other receiver parameters are established and the receiver is completely initialized.
A channel or hardware reset command resets WR3 D0 and disables the receiver.
MAME sets the Sync/Hunt bit of read register 0x00 when WR3 D4 is 1 or when the receiver is disabled (D0 = 0).
MAME's channel reset, z80scc_channel::device_reset, keeps WR3 D0 and clears every other bit of WR3, with m_wr3 &= 0x01.
WR4 contains the control bits for both the receiver and the transmitter.
These bits should be set in the transmit and receiver initialization routine before issuing the contents of WR1, WR3, WR6 and WR7.
On the ESCC, with the Extended Read option enabled, this register is read as RR4.
WR4 D7-D6 select the Clock Rate, the multiplier between clock and data rates: 00 X1, 01 X16, 10 X32, 11 X64.
In synchronous modes the 1X mode is forced internally and the Clock Rate bits are ignored, unless External Sync mode is selected.
In External Sync mode, 1X and 16X specify that only the /SYNC pin achieves character synchronization.
In External Sync mode, 32X lets either the /SYNC pin or a match with the WR7 character signal synchronization, the sync character being six or eight bits per WR10.
In External Sync mode, 64X puts receiver and transmitter in SDLC mode, with /SYNC used to start or stop a frame as if a flag had arrived.
WR4 stores D5-D4, the SYNC Mode selection: 00 Monosync, 01 Bisync, 10 SDLC, 11 External Sync; they are ignored unless synchronous modes are selected in the stop bits field.
In Monosync mode the receiver synchronizes on the WR7 character, the transmitter uses WR6 as time fill, and the sync character is six or eight bits by WR10.
In Monosync mode with Sync Character Load Inhibit set, the receiver strips the contents of WR6 from the data stream if received within character boundaries.
In Bisync mode WR7 joined with WR6 is the receive sync and transmit time fill, 12 or 16 bits received by WR10; the transmitted character is always 16 bits.
In SDLC mode a Flag (01111110) must be written to WR7, the receiver address field to WR6, and the SDLC CRC polynomial is selected in WR5.
In External Sync mode the SCC expects external logic to signal character synchronization on /SYNC; the crystal oscillator option in WR11 forces the internal /SYNC signal to 0.
In External Sync mode the transmitter is in Monosync mode using WR6 as time fill, with the sync character length given by the 6-bit/8-bit Sync bit in WR10.
WR4 stores D3-D2, the Stop Bits selection: 00 synchronous modes enable, 01 one stop bit, 10 one and a half, 11 two stop bits per transmitted character.
The receiver always checks for one stop bit in asynchronous mode.
A special mode specifies that a synchronous mode is selected, in which bits D4, D5, D6 and D7 apply and the 1X clock mode is forced internally.
The 1 1/2 stop bits mode is not used with the 1X clock mode.
WR4 D2 is always set to 1 by a channel or hardware reset, to ensure the /SYNC pin is in a known state after a reset.
WR4 stores D1, the Parity Even/Odd select: 1 selects even parity, 0 odd; the bit is ignored if Parity Enable is not set.
WR4 stores D0, Parity Enable; when set, an additional bit beyond the bits per character is added to transmitted data and expected in received data.
The received parity bit is transferred to the CPU as part of the data unless eight bits per character is selected in the receiver.
MAME's get_clock_mode derives the multiplier from D7-D6 alone, so it does not force 1X for synchronous modes.
MAME's channel reset, z80scc_channel::device_reset, stores 0x04 in the whole of WR4, so every bit but D2 is cleared.
WR5 contains control bits that affect the operation of the transmitter; D2 affects both the transmitter and the receiver.
With the Extended Read option enabled, WR5 is read as RR5.
WR5 D7, Data Terminal Ready, controls /DTR//REQ in DTR mode (selected in WR14): set makes /DTR Low, reset High; it is ignored when the pin acts as /REQ.
WR5 D7 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
WR5 stores D6-D5, the Transmit Bits/Character select: 00 five or less, 01 seven, 10 six, 11 eight; the table header prints Bit 7 and Bit 6.
Bits sent must be right justified with the least significant bits first.
Five or fewer bits per character must be formatted as in Table 5-5; in the six and seven bit modes, unused data bits are ignored.
For five or fewer bits the data byte carries a marker pattern of 1s and 0s above the data bits, from one up to five data bits.
WR5 stores D4, Send Break; when set it forces TxD to send continuous 0s from the next transmit clock, whether or not the transmitter is enabled.
When Send Break is reset, TxD continues to send the contents of the Transmit Shift register, which might be syncs, data or all 1s.
If Send Break is set in the mode printed 'X21' (Monosync and Loop) and the receiver gains character sync, the bit resets itself and the transmitter sends syncs or data.
WR5 D4 is also reset by a channel or hardware reset.
WR5 stores D3, Transmit Enable; data is not transmitted until set, and TxD sends continuous 1s unless Auto Echo or SDLC Loop mode is selected.
If Transmit Enable is reset after transmission starts, data or sync characters in progress are completed; disabled during a CRC character, sync or flag characters are sent instead.
WR5 D3 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
WR5 stores D2, the SDLC/CRC-16 polynomial select used by both transmitter and receiver: set selects CRC-16, reset the SDLC polynomial.
The SDLC/CRC polynomial is selected when SDLC mode is selected; the CRC generator and checker can be preset to all 0s or all 1s by the Preset bit in WR10.
WR5 D1, Request To Send, controls the /RTS pin: when set /RTS goes Low, when reset it goes High.
With Auto Enable in asynchronous mode, /RTS goes Low as RTS is set; on reset it stays Low until the transmitter is empty and the last stop bit has left.
In synchronous modes /RTS follows the state of the RTS bit directly, except in SDLC mode under the flag-on-underrun conditions of WR10 and WR7'.
WR5 D1 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
WR5 stores D0, Transmit CRC Enable; set when a character is loaded from the transmit buffer into the Transmit Shift register, CRC is calculated on that character.
The CRC is not automatically sent unless this bit is set when the transmit underrun exists.
On RTS reset MAME raises /RTS at once unless Auto Enables is set and RR1 shows not all sent, in any mode; the check runs when WR5 is written.
MAME's channel reset, z80scc_channel::device_reset, stores 0x00 in the whole of WR5, so D6, D5, D2 and D0 are cleared as well as D7, D4, D3 and D1.
WR6 stores the transmit sync character in Monosync mode, or the first byte of a 16-bit sync character in External Sync mode, as printed.
WR6 is not used in asynchronous modes.
In the SDLC modes WR6 stores the secondary address field, used to compare against the address field of the SDLC frame.
In SDLC mode the SCC does not automatically transmit the station address at the beginning of a response frame.
The bit positions of WR6 are shown in Figure 5-8.
WR7 stores the receive sync character in Monosync mode, the last eight bits of a 16-bit Bisync sync character, or a Flag (01111110) in SDLC modes.
WR7 holds the receive sync character or a flag if one of the special versions of the External Sync mode is selected.
WR7 is not used in Asynchronous mode.
The bit positions of WR7 are shown in Figure 5-9.
On the ESCC and the 85C30 with WR15 D0 set, MAME stores the byte written to WR7 in its WR7' variable; otherwise it stores it in the sync pattern.
WR8 is the transmit buffer register.
A byte written to WR8 is written to the transmit buffer.
WR9 is the Master Interrupt Control register and contains the Reset command bits.
Only one WR9 exists in the SCC, and it is written from either channel.
The interrupt control bits are programmed together with the Reset command because only a hardware reset resets them.
WR9 D7-D6 select the reset command: 00 null, 01 Channel Reset B, 10 Channel Reset A, 11 Force Hardware Reset; the capture prints 0 as O in the null code.
A reset command in WR9 disables the channel's receiver and transmitter, forces TxD marking and the modem controls High, resets all IPs and IUSs and disables all its interrupts.
Four extra PCLK cycles must be allowed after any reset command before more commands or controls are written to the channel.
The Null command (00) has no effect; it is used when a write to WR9 is needed for a reason other than a reset command.
The Channel Reset B command (01) performs a channel reset on Channel B.
The Channel Reset A command (10) performs a channel reset on Channel A.
Force Hardware Reset (11) acts as a hardware reset, except that the Shift Right/Shift Left bit is unchanged and the MIE, Status High/Low and DLC bits take the programmed values.
WR9 stores D5, Software Interrupt Acknowledge; when set, reading RR2 executes an interrupt acknowledge cycle internally.
A software acknowledge makes the INT pin return High, the IEO pin go Low and sets the IUS latch for the highest priority interrupt pending.
The Software Interrupt Acknowledge bit is reserved on NMOS and always writes as 0.
WR9 stores D4, Status High/Status Low: set, the SCC modifies vector bits V6-V4 per Table 5-6; reset, bits V1-V3; it governs the vector of an acknowledge cycle and RR2B.
WR9 D4 is reset by a hardware reset.
Table 5-6 lists, for Channel B and Channel A, the transmit buffer empty, external/status change, receive character available and special receive condition codes 000 to 111.
WR9 stores D3, Master Interrupt Enable; set to 1 it globally enables interrupts, and cleared to 0 it disables them.
Clearing MIE forces the IEO pin to follow IEI unless an IUS bit is set; no IUS bit is set after MIE is cleared.
WR9 D3 is reset by a hardware reset.
WR9 stores D2, Disable Lower Chain, with which the CPU controls the daisy chain: set to 1 it forces IEO Low, stopping lower priority devices from requesting interrupts.
WR9 D2 is reset by a hardware reset.
WR9 stores D1, No Vector select; when set, no vector is returned during an interrupt acknowledge cycle even if the SCC is the highest priority requester.
WR9 stores D0, Vector Includes Status; when set the returned vector varies with the highest priority IP set; the bit is ignored if No Vector is set.
Table 5-5 shows the encoding of the status information.
MAME's hardware reset keeps WR9 D5-D2, so Status High/Status Low (D4) keeps its value, and sets D7-D6 to 11 and D1-D0 to 0.
MAME's hardware reset keeps WR9 D5-D2, so Master Interrupt Enable (D3) keeps its value.
MAME's hardware reset keeps WR9 D5-D2, so Disable Lower Chain (D2) keeps its value.
WR10 contains miscellaneous control bits for both the receiver and the transmitter.
On the ESCC with the Extended Read option enabled, WR10 may be read as RR11.
WR10 stores D7, the CRC Presets I/O select: set, the CRC generator and checker are preset to 1; reset, they are preset to 0.
Either preset can be used with either CRC polynomial; in SDLC mode the transmitted CRC is inverted and the received CRC is checked against 0001110100001111.
WR10 D7 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
WR10 D7 is ignored in asynchronous mode.
WR10 stores D6-D5, the Data Encoding select for both transmitter and receiver: 00 NRZ, 01 NRZI, 10 FM1 (transition = 1), 11 FM0 (transition = 0).
All clocking options are available for all coding methods; the DPLL helps recover clocking in NRZI and FM modes, and any method can be used in X1 mode.
A hardware reset forces NRZ mode, and the timing of the modes is shown in Figure 5-13.
WR10 stores D4, Go-Active-On-Poll; in SDLC Loop mode, with an EOP received, it lets the transmitter go active and on-loop.
On selecting SDLC Loop mode, the SCC links RxD to TxD with only gate delays until this bit is set and an EOP arrives; then it goes on-loop.
In SDLC Loop mode, if this bit is set as a flag leaves the shift register, another flag or data byte follows; otherwise the SCC reverts to 1-bit delay.
To transmit a single response frame, reset this bit after the first data byte but before CRC; if not reset before CRC, extra flags slow the loop response.
After gaining control of the loop the SCC cannot transmit again until a flag and another EOP arrive; good practice is to set this bit only on a poll frame.
In synchronous modes other than SDLC with Loop Mode set, this bit is set before the transmitter goes active on a received sync character.
WR10 D4 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
WR10 D4 is always ignored in asynchronous mode, and in synchronous modes unless Loop Mode is set.
WR10 stores D3, Mark/Flag Idle line control, which affects only SDLC: 0 sends flags as the idle line, 1 sends continuous 1s after the closing flag.
The idle line is chosen byte by byte, a flag or eight 1s; a loop's primary station should use Mark Idle to create the EOP, deselected before frame data.
The Mark/Flag Idle bit is ignored in Loop mode, but its programmed value takes effect on exiting Loop mode.
WR10 D3 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
On the ESCC with Automatic Tx SDLC Flag (WR7' D0 = 1; printed WRT, 00=1) the bit can stay mark idle; opening flag, closing flag and mark idle are automatic.
WR10 stores D2, Abort/Flag On Underrun select; it affects only SDLC: set, a transmit underrun sends an abort and a flag instead of CRC; reset, it sends CRC.
At the start of that 16-bit transmission the Transmit Underrun/EOM bit is set, causing an External/Status interrupt, and a Transmit Buffer Empty interrupt occurs at its end.
With Abort/Flag On Underrun and Mark/Flag Idle both 1, all 1s follow an underrun; the bit should be set after the first data byte and reset immediately after the last.
This bit is ignored in Loop mode, but its programmed value is active on exiting Loop mode.
WR10 D2 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
WR10 stores D1, Loop Mode control; in SDLC mode its initial set connects TxD to RxD and starts searching the incoming data so the SCC can go on loop.
Select Loop mode after setting the other SDLC bits and before enabling transmitter and receiver; the SCC goes on-loop when Go-Active-On-Poll is set and an EOP arrives.
If Loop Mode is reset after the SCC goes on-loop, the SCC waits for the next EOP to go off-loop.
In synchronous modes the SCC uses this bit with Go-Active-On-Poll to synchronize the transmitter to the receiver; the receiver should not be enabled until after the mode is selected.
TxD is held marking in that mode unless a break is programmed; the receiver waits for a sync character, then enables the transmitter and removes any break.
Loop mode works with sync characters of 6, 8 or 16 bits.
WR10 D1 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
WR10 D1 is ignored in asynchronous mode.
WR10 stores D0, the 6-Bit/8-Bit SYNC select: set in Monosync mode, receiver and transmitter sync characters are six bits instead of eight; in Bisync, the received sync is 12 bits.
In Bisync mode the transmitter sync character remains 16 bits; the bit is ignored in SDLC and asynchronous modes but still has effect in the special external sync modes.
WR10 D0 is reset by a channel or hardware reset.
